home.heading: Mausritter Tools
home.leadHtml: A collection of browser-based helpers for running and playing Mausritter.
home.noServerHtml: Everything runs entirely in your browser — there is no server and nothing is uploaded.
home.settlementItemHtml: Settlement generator — rolls a whole mouse settlement: who governs it, what they trade, what is happening as the players arrive, plus every shop with its keeper, quirks and priced stock. Lock what you like, re-roll the rest, then share it as a link or print it.

about.heading: About
about.leadHtml: Mausritter Tools is a small set of browser-based helpers for Mausritter, the tabletop roleplaying game of brave mice by Isaac Williams.

howItWorks.heading: How it works
paragraphsHtml: The whole app is a static site that runs in your browser. There is no server, no account and no analytics, and nothing you generate is uploaded anywhere. A settlement is produced purely from its seed, so the same link always rebuilds the same settlement.

Locking a value freezes it in place so that re-rolling everything else leaves it alone. Editing a value locks it too. Because locks and hand edits would make a link unwieldy, the address bar carries only the seed and the generator settings; the full state travels through the JSON export, and is kept in your browser's local storage between visits.

official.heading: What is official, and what is not
paragraphsHtml: The settlement tables, the tavern table, the non-player mice tables, gear prices, hirelings and spells are all taken from the Mausritter SRD, which is published under CC BY 4.0. They are imported directly from the SRD source rather than retyped, so the wording is the author's own.

Mausritter has no shops or services table. The SRD says only that taverns appear in hamlets and larger, that warbands can be recruited in a town or city, that human-made goods are found near human populations, that a bank charges 1% to retrieve what it holds, that repairs cost 10% of an item's price per usage dot, and that “the size of the settlement determines what types of hireling are available” without ever saying how. Everything else about shops in this tool — which services exist, how size gates them, their stock, quirks and names — is an unofficial house rule original to this project. Each shop shows the SRD rule it was extrapolated from, so you can see where the line falls.
Mouse names are also original. The SRD contains no name tables, and the lists used by the official generator are not published under a licence that permits reuse.

translation.heading: About the German edition
paragraphsHtml: The German version of this tool is an unofficial fan translation by the mausritter-tools contributors. It is not the official German edition of Mausritter, is not endorsed by Losing Games, and no official German translation was used as a source. CC BY 4.0 permits translation as long as the change is declared, which is what this notice does.

A settlement does not change when you change language. Every table is translated row for row, so the same seed produces the same place in both languages and a link shared between a German and an English player shows the same settlement — only the words differ.

itemCards.heading: About the item cards
paragraphsHtml: The printable item cards copy the layout and the drawings of the official Mausritter item cards. The Mausritter Third Party Licence expressly permits third-party creators to use, copy and modify the item card templates and item card art, and this tool does exactly that. The drawings are by Isaac Williams and are taken from the official Item Card Studio; they are unaltered, and a card only carries one where the item is the very thing the drawing shows. Everything else on the card — which items get cards at all, and what each one says — is generated by this tool and is not official.

The cards are set in Texturina and Open Sans, both under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, which is shipped alongside them. The official cards use Open Sans Condensed, which has since been withdrawn and folded back into Open Sans as its narrow width; this tool uses that narrow width instead.
Cards are sized in whole inventory slots, so printing the sheet at 100% gives cards that sit on a real Mausritter character sheet.

diceTable.heading: About the dice table
paragraphsHtml: The dice table connects the browsers at your table directly to one another, encrypted, with no server in between and nothing written down anywhere. A table code is not an account: it is the name your browsers use to find each other, and anybody holding it can listen in, so pass it around the way you would pass around a door key. Close the tab and the table stops existing.

Every named roll is a rule printed in the Mausritter SRD, not a house rule: a save is a d20 at or under the attribute, an attack always lands and rolls the weapon's die, a spell is a d6 for each point of power with usage marked on every 4, 5 or 6 and a miscast on every 6, and a new mouse's attribute is 3d6 keeping the best two. Rolls the book does not define are not offered — there is no critical hit, no morale roll and no reaction roll here, because Mausritter has none. The notation box covers whatever else your table rolls.

Nothing decides what a result means for your sheet. A miscast is counted, never applied, and a usage dot is announced, never filled in. Each roll carries the seed that produced it, so a roll can be pasted to somebody whose browser could not reach the table and rebuilt there exactly.

source.heading: Source
paragraphsHtml: The code, the imported tables and the importer script are on GitHub.

support.heading: Support Mausritter
paragraphsHtml: This tool is no substitute for the game. Mausritter is pay-what-you-want in digital form and well worth owning: mausritter.com.

dice.heading: Dice table
dice.leadHtml: Roll where the whole party can see it. The dice go straight from one browser to another — there is no server, and nothing is kept.
dice.statusAway: Not at a table — these rolls are only on this screen.
dice.statusFailed: This browser would not open a connection. Rolls still work here; they just stay here.
dice.nameNeeded: Put a name in first, so the rest of the table knows whose dice those were.
dice.notationBad: That is not a roll this understands. Try d20, 2d6+1, or 3d6kh2 to keep the best two of three.
dice.tableBad: That is not a table code.
dice.inviteHint: Anyone with this link joins the table. Anyone with this code can listen to it, so share it the way you would share a door key.
dice.secretHint: A private roll tells the table that you rolled and nothing else. The dice never leave this browser.
dice.edgeHint: A save made with advantage rolls two d20s and keeps the lower, because low is what passes; disadvantage keeps the higher. An impaired attack rolls d4 and an enhanced one d12, whatever the weapon. Mausritter has one step of each, so there is nothing to stack.
dice.spellHint: Casting reports what the dice showed, not what to do about it: one usage mark for every 4, 5 or 6, and a miscast for every 6. Read your spell's effect with [DICE] as the number of dice you cast with and [SUM] as the total. Filling the dots in is still your job.
dice.privacyHint: Rolls travel straight between browsers, encrypted, with no server in the middle and nothing stored anywhere. Close the tab and the table is gone.
dice.reachHint: Some networks will not let two browsers talk directly, and there is no relay to fall back on. If somebody never appears, paste them the seed beside a roll — it rebuilds the same dice anywhere.

readings.spell/cast: Read [DICE] as {count} and [SUM] as the total.

readings.mouse/attribute: Attribute score — roll again for each of STR, DEX and WIL.

fantasiaArchive.exportTitle: Download this settlement as a Fantasia Archive project folder, zipped
fantasiaArchive.readMeTitle: Importing this settlement into Fantasia Archive
readMeSteps: Unzip this file. Inside is a folder called {folder}.
Open the Fantasia Archive project you want the settlement added to.
Save that project first, with Project → Save current project. Merging cannot be undone.
Choose Project → Advanced → Merge another project into the current one.
Select the {folder} folder itself, not the files inside it.
fantasiaArchive.readMeWarning: Do not put anything else in the {folder} folder. Fantasia Archive reads every file in it as a database, so a stray note or screenshot will break the import. That is exactly why these instructions are outside the folder rather than in it.
fantasiaArchive.readMeNote: The settlement arrives as a Location, with its tavern and shops as buildings inside it, numbered as they are on the map. Their keepers arrive as Characters and their stock as Items, all linked to each other. The settlement also quietly carries the seed it was generated from, so you can bring it back: save the project out of Fantasia Archive again and import that folder into the settlement generator.
fantasiaArchive.readMeMapNote: The map is already there. It is drawn into the settlement's own description, above the licence notice, with the numbered key written out beneath it. You do not have to do anything to see it.
fantasiaArchive.readMeMapFileNote: Beside this note is {map}, the same map as an image file. Fantasia Archive's PDF export cannot include the embedded copy, so if you want the map in an exported PDF, edit the settlement's description, use the toolbar's image button, choose "Local image", and pick {map} from wherever you unzipped it. Leave it where it is or move it somewhere else entirely — anywhere except into the {folder} folder.
fantasiaArchive.readMeVersionNote: Written for Fantasia Archive v1, the format every released version reads.
